I find the "what is downvoat" question tends to get a little over-complicated by most people. While this is good because it shows they're thinking about it, it can be bad because it makes it hard to actually reach some kind of consensus.

If you think about what a downvoat does (add weight to content to move it up or down a list) it gets a little easier. From here, it's easy to see that the impetus for voating either way should be to make stuff visible first compared to other content on the same list.

"A reminder to myself and a notice to other website users that I personally found a post or comment objectionable or not contributing to the current conversation."

IE my own personal opinion just like everyone else. At least I want to vote that way.

I understand that upvoting is meant for promoting comments or posts which add to some discussion, while downvoating is meant to demote comments or post which don't. I don't personally feel comfortable within those guidelines at all. I don't personally want anyone else's votes to affect what is shown when I open a post to dig into the comment section, nor do I want any other users' website view to be altered by how I vote.

For me personally, I think there is a serious problem with the "karma" mechanism that many websites employ. I think it actually stifles true discussion and contains listeners in a bubble. I think it might make town-hall participants more focused on gaining points rather than actually contributing, or discarding valid opinions because the speaker hasn't excelled in a certain point system.
